title: Providers: Anthropic, OpenAI and Google — keys, limits and cost

videos.script: Three providers, three SDKs, one idea. A system instruction, a conversation, a limit, a reply with token counts. {{shapes}} The names differ, and the differences are where code breaks when it moves. Then what running against any of them involves. A key that stays out of the code. {{keys}} A rate limit you can see coming in the headers, and the queue your own machine makes. Retries the SDK makes for you, and where they stop. {{retries}} One workload priced at ten models, a factor of twenty-four between the ends. {{costs}} And an adapter with a fallback, tested by breaking the first provider, and a hole in it found with one line of Python. {{fallback}} No provider is called and nothing is spent. The SDKs talk to the model on your computer. What only a provider does comes from its documentation.
